key_insight: UPA reframes prompt optimization as a tree-based search that finds high-quality prompts using unsupervised selection signals instead of relying on labeled reward feedback. This enables automated, structured prompt refinement when supervised rewards are unavailable.
problem_solved: Removes the dependence on supervised reward signals for automated prompt optimization, allowing prompt agents to search and select effective prompts in practical, unlabeled settings.
method: Construct a structured prompt space as a tree and perform iterative expansion/search over candidate prompt branches.
Score and prune branches using unsupervised selection criteria (e.g., self-consistency/consensus, diversity, uncertainty, language-model-based fluency/coherence) rather than labeled rewards.
Iteratively refine and select promising prompts via tree-based planning (expansion, evaluation, selection) to produce robust final prompts.
impact: Enables practitioners to automate prompt tuning in domains where labeled feedback is scarce or expensive, reducing manual engineering and allowing scalable prompt discovery for downstream tasks.
visual_elements: Tree diagram showing prompt-space expansion: root = seed prompt, branches = candidate edits, highlighted final path.
Pipeline flowchart: generate candidates → unsupervised scoring → prune/select → iterate.
Icon set illustrating unsupervised metrics: consensus/majority, diversity, uncertainty, fluency.
Before/after schematic comparing manual prompt vs. UPA-refined prompt (qualitative examples).
paper_title: UPA: Unsupervised Prompt Agent via Tree-Based Search and Selection
paper_authors: Siran Peng, Weisong Zhao, Tianyu Fu, Chenxu Zhao, Tianshuo Zhang
